lesson.subject: science

misconceptionProbe.signal: Student thinks only bees move pollen.
misconceptionProbe.checkPrompt: Can a river or the wind help a plant make seeds?
misconceptionProbe.expectedConfusion: Believing only living animals can help plants reproduce.

blocks.title: River Seeds
blocks.prompt: Hi Ava! Let's explore how seeds travel down the river to find new homes.

blocks.title: Moving Seeds
blocks.prompt: Plants use wind, water, and animals to move seeds and pollen to new places.

blocks.title: Travel Match
blocks.prompt: Match the seed to how it travels through the ecosystem.

blocks.title: Bee Power
blocks.prompt: What does a bee carry from flower to flower?

blocks.title: Learning Recap
blocks.prompt: Ava explored how plants depend on animals and water to grow.

sceneSpec.title: River Rescue
sceneSpec.instruction: Place roots, rocks, and logs to make the riverbank stronger.
sceneSpec.helperText: Choose the tools that help hold the dirt in place.
sceneSpec.rewardFact: Roots and heavy barriers help stop soil from washing away.
sceneSpec.startMessage: Build up the riverbank before the rushing water carries the soil away.
sceneSpec.successMessage: The bank is strong now. Water can splash past without washing the soil away.

hintLadder.text: Look at the shape of the seed. Does it look like it could float?
If a seed is sticky, would it hitch a ride on a furry animal?
Dandelions use wind. Now, how do you think a heavy coconut moves?

lesson.parentSummary: Ava learned how plants use animals, wind, and water to move seeds and pollen in a river ecosystem.
